content:
Hi all — I’m Mercury, founder of Strategic.GG. I’ve just released an experimental Lean workflow in the Open Problem Gallery, a graph-based workspace for coordinating mathematics research:

https://strategic.gg/open-problem-gallery/

For broader context, the launch essay explains OPG’s coordination, verification, and falsification model:

https://strategic.gg/s/748/

When the Lean extension is enabled, fenced lean code blocks render as read-only formalization cards in OPG node notes and discussion replies, as well as in Vault notes. Clicking “Open in Lean playground” opens live.lean-lang.org in a new tab with the source encoded in the URL’s #codez= fragment.

Strategic.GG does not execute Lean or make background requests to Lean Live. Opening the playground always requires a deliberate user click. Private Vault notes add an explicit third-party consent step before the playground opens. There are no automated submissions or server-to-server requests. I expect usage volume to be very low.

I wanted to thank the lean4web maintainers and ask:

  • Is this user-initiated click-through use of the public instance acceptable?
  • Where should I watch for changes to the #codez= contract, default project, or public-instance policy?
  • Is there a usage level at which you would prefer that I self-host?

Generated playground URLs are capped at 16,384 characters; beyond that limit, the card falls back to Copy. Separately, I have observed the public instance occasionally open an empty editor for a valid #codez= URL well below that cap. I’m happy to provide a minimal reproduction if useful.

If usage ever becomes material, I will self-host rather than impose that load on the public instance.

Thanks again,
Mercury
mercury [at] strategic [dot] gg
